To begin, how would you best describe your history with competitive movement and training?
Options: [A lifelong athlete, consistently training and competing in organized team or individual sports. | An active life with a focus on functional movement, gym work, and self-directed challenges. | A return to high-performance sport after focusing on other life pursuits; ready to test my limits.]
A lifelong athlete, consistently training and competing in organized team or individual sports.

Looking back on your experience, what element of competition has historically been the biggest driver for your performance?
Options: [The raw, immediate thrill of explosive power and reactive speed. | The psychological challenge and deep physical discipline of sustained endurance and tactical pacing. | The relentless pursuit of technical precision and complex motor coordination.]
The psychological challenge and deep physical discipline of sustained endurance and tactical pacing.

As you look toward the next chapter of your high-performance sport pathway, which environment do you feel would best elevate your potential?
Options: [A data-driven, professional squad environment with constant performance tracking and high-tech support. | A rugged, self-reliant training regime that centers on mental fortitude and internal mastery. | A collaborative, strategy-focused team setting that values tactical synergy and mentorship.]
A data-driven, professional squad environment with constant performance tracking and high-tech support.
Before we finalize your profile, is there a specific, defining moment in your athletic history—a particular victory or a hard-won lesson—that still shapes how you approach your training today?
Winning my first Deaflympic gold taught me that while the starting pistol is silent to me, my drive to break 46 seconds is deafening.
